- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ba2440b7417eb2e21ac987bcf1c81dedcc502c39` — the merge of head `20d149c6e88cce887bec9f7b7a3192d5771fd5df` into base `a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ba2440b7417eb2e21ac987bcf1c81dedcc502c39 && git checkout ba2440b7417eb2e21ac987bcf1c81dedcc502c39
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d 20d149c6e88cce887bec9f7b7a3192d5771fd5df && git checkout -B drift-repro a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d && git merge --no-ff 20d149c6e88cce887bec9f7b7a3192d5771fd5df

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `20d149c6e88cce887bec9f7b7a3192d5771fd5df`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the PR body and changeset is true and complete against the diff. `ReplayNotFaithfulError` (`src/runner/driver.ts`, re-exported by `./runner` through `export * from './driver.js'`) is the only new exported name, and `AskTask.callTool` is the only new field on an exported type. Both are additive: the field is optional, a live driver ignores it, and a `RecordedDriver` given no `callTool` returns the recorded turn and sends nothing, exactly as before. `runHalf` and `QuestionResult` / `OperationResult` keep their shapes; `notMeasured` gains a third documented cause. The answer that moves is declared in the changeset: a `--driver recorded:FILE` replay now re-sends a question or operation turn's recorded writes (`create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `run_action`) to the booted app, in recorded order, as the turn's persona, so an `applied` operation reads back what the run wrote instead of a false "0 row(s) read back" fail. Reads are never re-sent, a recorded refusal must meet the same refusal (code, flow refusal, or codeless error), a created row's recorded id is remapped to the replay's id, and every divergence or unanswered recorded write throws `ReplayNotFaithfulError`, which `runHalf` records as NOT MEASURED naming the call, never a fail.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author writes (spec, app metadata) is added, narrowed or changed in meaning; the widening is an additive export and an optional field of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`, and no existing export is removed, renamed or narrowed in type.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no runtime or security behaviour of the platform. The re-sent writes go only to the replay's own freshly booted app, through the runner's MCP door with the persona's key, so they meet the same permission checks the recorded run met; a replay cannot write as anyone the recording did not act as. Live drivers are unchanged. The grader stays deterministic (cloud#3600 cost ruling).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-kv3s20`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
